transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-16 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (CISO, Elm Street), Liam O'Connor (Head of Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Legal)

Summary (auto gen - may be incomplete): Quick intake focused on security posture requirements for inference workloads. Elm Street evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; primary concerns are KMS/customer-managed keys, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention, and SOC2/ISO attestations.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, i'm Jordan with Redwood, this is priya who's our solutions engineer, quick intros?
[00:07] Maya: hi i'm maya, ciso at elm street, thanks. we own the security requirements for AI projects.
[00:11] Liam: liam here, platform, we run most infra in aws, some gcp for analytics.
[00:15] Sofia: sofia, legal, i'll be helping with contracts and data residency clauses.
[00:20] Priya: great, quick agenda — we want to understand current stack, data types, retention, and any hard compliance gates. then we'll go through the hosting options and what security controls map to each.
[00:30] Maya: sounds good. to start — we will have PHI in some prompts and also moderately sensitive PII. need to know if redwood hosted can support customer-managed keys, and if logs/audit trails are available to feed into our siem.
[00:45] Jordan: totally, good outline. so big picture question — are you open to a hosted api for an initial rollout or is private/dedicated required from day one?
[00:54] Maya: ideally we'd like to evaluate hosted first for speed, but contractually we have to prove we can isolate data and control keys — so customer-managed keys are a blocker unless there's a clear path.
[01:10] Liam: also latency matters, we do some near-real-time inference in support flows. if dedicated buys us better latency/cost, we want the numbers.
[01:20] Priya: note on keys: redwood supports customer-managed KMS in private deployments and dedicated has options for CMK via bring-your-own-kms in some setups — hosted supports envelope encryption today but not BYOK for full tenant key rotation in all regions. i'll clarify exact region coverage.
[01:37] Maya: when you say envelope, is the master key managed by redwood? can we rotate?
[01:42] Priya: correct — hosted uses our key hierarchy, customers can request key rotation windows, but full HSM BYOK where the CMK never leaves your control is available on private deployments and in some dedicated arrangements with enterprise contracts.
[01:58] Sofia: that's key for legal — we prefer either BYOK or an MSA clause that specifies rotation/custody. is there an HSM attestation?
[02:06] Jordan: yes, for private we can integrate with customer HSM or KMS via standard network flows; we can provide HSM attestation docs — i'll attach the relevant certs.
[02:15] Liam: another question: audit logs — we need per-token request tracing and retention for 7 years for some use cases; can you stream audit logs to our splunk or cloud logging?
[02:26] Priya: we offer audit logs and can stream to customer sinks (syslog, cloud logging) for dedicated/private. hosted offers logs via our console and exports, but long-term retention and push-based streaming is generally part of enterprise bundles. i should note that per-token logging may include masked content; we have controls for partial redaction at ingest.
[02:47] Maya: redaction is important — we can't export raw PHI. what's the approach for masking in transit?
[02:54] Priya: we do TLS in transit; for masking we support policy-based redaction on the agent before it's written to logs, and you can configure retention and redaction rules. in private deployments you can run the redaction service in your VPC so nothing leaves unmasked.
[03:09] Jordan: quick clarification, when you say "private deployment" — we mean private control plane with customer-managed networking and optional on-prem model hosting, correct?
[03:17] Liam: yes, that's what would satisfy our network team — VPC peering and no public endpoints.
[03:21] Priya: exactly — private allows full VPC-only access patterns, dedicated sits in our tenant but can be isolated, hosted is fully multi-tenant.
[03:31] Maya: on compliance: do you have SOC 2 and ISO 27001? direct question.
[03:35] Jordan: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications — i'll drop the latest reports.
[03:40] Sofia: do you allow us to run a third-party pen test against a dedicated environment?
[03:45] Priya: for dedicated and private yes — typically we allow security assessments under an NDA, scope agreed up front; hosted pen tests are limited for obvious multi-tenant concerns.
[03:55] Liam: ok noted. data residency — we have EU customers, need inference to stay in eu region for some models. does redwood support region pinning?
[04:03] Jordan: yes, region and model pinning supported across dedicated/private. hosted has regional endpoints; i'll map which regions have which verified models.
[04:12] Maya: another thing — RBAC and SSO. we use SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. we need role separation and auditability.
[04:20] Priya: we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM on enterprise tiers; RBAC is fine-grained — you can restrict per-route and per-model, and there's token-level auditing. sometimes the SCIM schema needs a mapping; our Okta/AD integrations typically take an afternoon to set up.
[04:38] Sofia: contractually we need a retention schedule built into the DPA. our baseline is 7 years for audit logs and 3 years for inference artifacts, unless specifically exempted. is that feasible?
[04:50] Jordan: that's doable for dedicated/private, hosted would need an enterprise addendum for extended log retention. we'll flag that in the follow-up.
[04:58] Maya: any colleagues we should bring to the technical deep dive? platform and infra?
[05:02] Liam: yes i'll bring our infra lead and our security ops engineer — they will want to validate SIEM integration and key rotation automation.
[05:10] Priya: we'll prepare a runbook: network diagrams, example terraform for VPC peering, and a checklist for SIEM ingestion.
[05:17] Maya: ok one more — are model artifacts and weights ever stored unencrypted at rest?
[05:23] Priya: all model weights are encrypted at rest; in private you can control the KMS. for hosted, we use disk encryption plus application-level encryption.
[05:31] Jordan: i want to call out a typical tradeoff we see: hosted is fastest to get started but narrower BYOK and long-term retention options; dedicated gives more isolation and retention flexibility, while private is full control but comes with setup time and ops responsibility.
[05:52] Maya: that matches our internal security posture. we'd probably want to pilot hosted to move fast only if we can validate logs and masking, otherwise dedicated seems safer.
[06:01] Sofia: liability question — if a breach occurs at redwood-hosted level, how does indemnity look?
[06:07] Jordan: indemnity is something we will cover in the MSA; for enterprise deals we negotiate security liability clauses — i'll loop in legal on that.
[06:15] Maya: ok good. can you clarify token-level cost and whether logs for every request will materially change billing?
[06:22] Priya: logging doesn't change token billing; billing is per-token inference. audit log storage and export may have a separate charge under extended retention.
[06:30] Liam: operational question — KV cache, do you persist any user prefixes or are those ephemeral? we want to ensure PII isn't cached long-term.
[06:39] Priya: KV cache is in-memory by default, ephemeral between sessions, but there are configurable cache persistence options for performance; we'll disable persistence for any PII workflows.
[06:49] Maya: great. any red flags from your side?
[06:52] Priya: just to note, if you need BYOK in hosted for EU region immediately it might be a gap — but we can provide bridging options (dedicated in region or private).
[07:03] Jordan: next steps recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO attestation, network diagram, security deck, and a dedicated pricing sheet. priya will share POC checklist and terraform snippets.
[07:15] Maya: i'll get you our retention requirements and a list of regulated datasets.
[07:19] Sofia: legal will review the MSA template and flag clauses — we'll want to see specific KMS language.
[07:24] Jordan: excellent. shall we tentatively put the technical deep dive for w/c 2026-07-27?
[07:29] Liam: that works for our team.
[07:32] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs.
[07:35] Priya: thanks, bye.
